checklist.detail: NARloy-Z Copper Alloy (Cu-Ag-Zr): only 11% thermal margin (computed wall temp 722 K vs 800 K max). Thin margin. Basis: coupled throat wall balance: gas h_g ~11.5 kW/m2K incl. carbon-deposit credit, T_aw ~3577 K, coolant ~37 m/s (coolant-side wall ~671 K), 0.50 mm wall. Levers that lower it: faster coolant (Coolant velocity; SP-8087 caps liquids at ~61 m/s, at a jacket-dP cost), a thinner wall, a liner rated hotter or more conductive (e.g. GRCop-84), or more film cooling.

checklist.detail: Hottest wall station is in the convergent section (area ratio ~1.0, regen): wall ~738 K, 1.08x that section's material limit (warns below 1.15x, like the throat row). Levers: more chamber film (or a convergent film ring for the throat region), faster coolant, a thinner or more conductive liner, or extend active cooling.

checklist.detail: Near the end of active cooling (area ratio ~21.4), estimated jacket/coolant pressure (~13.4 MPa) exceeds local hot-gas static pressure (~0.0 MPa) - the net load on the channel-land wall there REVERSES direction. Modeled as a clamped-strip bending stress across the ~9.8 mm channel width, this reversed ~13.4 MPa differential is ~2555 MPa against a ~133 MPa allowable (Inconel 718 Nickel Superalloy, SF 1.5) - but this is a coarse clamped-plate-strip proxy, NOT a real buckling/FEA analysis, and this codebase has no real-engine spot check for it yet. Treat this as 'worth a closer structural look', not a validated failure prediction. Consider more/narrower channels (smaller span), tapering the actively-cooled length, or a thicker wall there.
